title: Darkness Comes Rattling - a game that flew under my radar!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qrag4Jg-veo

Daniel (@dungeondive) found Darkness Comes Rattling while researching Kevin Wilson for Arkham Horror coverage, nine years after its 2015 release, and opens by declaring it the best board game title ever awarded to anything. It is a cooperative game he plays solo with three heroes, which he calls the sweet spot because challenges come in three flavours — mind, body and spirit — and matching a hero to a challenge is how you earn the right to roll.

The premise is a serpent that has swallowed the sun. The sun creeps down the snake's length, and when it is fully digested you lose. Tribal heroes range out through four regions winning challenges for equipment, bones to spend at merchants and the four legendary wind items, until the sun reaches a horn space and the party nominates its bravest to enter the snake's mouth and race the digestion.

Two mechanisms get his praise. Corruption tokens carry a colour and a number, and a matching die result is cancelled outright, so the board slowly eats your dice. And the darkness track is a timer you can stand on and interact with, which he rates far above an arbitrary clock. Components are frankly mass-market — his board split from its backing and needed glue — but he paid about twenty dollars and has lost all three games so far.

----

Daniel praises the sun track for being a place on the board as well as a countdown — which other games make their timer somewhere you can actually go, and does that genuinely beat a plain clock?
